title: The bus speaks TCP between boxes and on Windows
intention: The bus carries messages over TCP between boxes and on Windows, while staying on Unix sockets inside a Linux box, so a device on akiendell can reach a bus and the buses on two boxes can reach each other.
why: Python on Windows has no socket.AF_UNIX (measured 2026-11-04 on akiendell: the web server died at cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py:95), so no device on a Windows box can reach any bus; and buses on two boxes (outline 5.4.2.8.1) can only reach each other over the network. Akien 2026-11-04: 'yes please' (outline 5.4.2.11.4).
traces_to: Outline 5.4.2.8 (one bus per cairn instance, extended across hosts), 5.4.2.8.1 (a bus per box, the buses talk) and 5.4.2.11.4 (TCP between boxes and on Windows); Telos: running multiple heavy tasks at once across Akien's boxes; Law 3 (the transport choice is settled by measuring, 5.4.2.11).
how: Give the bus an address that is either a Unix socket path or host:port. server.py:523 also listens on TCP 127.0.0.1 beside bus.sock (on Windows, where there is no AF_UNIX); no bus ever listens on the LAN; remote.py exchange() picks the transport from the address (AF_UNIX where it exists and the bus is on this box, TCP otherwise). Same wire format (one JSON request, one JSON reply), so callers do not change. Box to box rides ssh (open-4d72b5d4dbe0, Akien 2026-11-04: 'host fingerprinting with ssh sounds good'): the joining box forwards a local port to the home box's bus over ssh with the host key checked (StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, the home's key in known_hosts), e.g. ssh -N -L 127.0.0.1:<port>:<home bus.sock> <home>; the local bus address then names that port. ssh is the gate; no token. Measure TCP loopback latency against the 50 us Unix socket number (5.4.2.11.1). BUILDER BRIEF: A Haiku builder needs: (1) the files: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py (listener at :523), cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/__main__.py:23, cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py (exchange at :87-104, _spawn :147, _setsid :197); (2) the port: env CAIRN_BUS_TCP_PORT, default 7419 (unassigned by IANA), checked free at build; (3) the selection rule above, verbatim; (4) that the wire format must not change; (5) the Windows spawn flags DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW as in launchers/superclaude _sc_spawn_detached; (6) the gate is ssh with a checked host key (open-4d72b5d4dbe0 answered), the tunnel started by the bus client's lazy start on a box whose CAIRN_HOME_HOST is another box; (7) proofs in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/ and cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/, a tooth that forces the TCP path on Linux (AF_UNIX hidden) so it is provable here; (8) the latency bench is scratch today (5.4.2.11.1), so record numbers in the ticket, not a new tool.
falsifier: Done when (a) on akiendell, a fresh python using cairn.tools.bus_client.remote.RemoteBus().list() gets an answer from a bus it lazily started, over TCP 127.0.0.1, no AF_UNIX error; (b) from akiendell a request reaches the bus on akiendelllinux through an ssh tunnel with the host key checked, and a tunnel to a host whose key does not match is refused, and nothing on akiendelllinux listens on the LAN for the bus; (c) on Linux the Unix-socket p50 round trip stays within 10% of the 50 us measured at outline 5.4.2.11.1, and TCP loopback is measured and recorded. Horizon: the first box-to-box message. Wrong intent if ssh cannot carry it from Windows (OpenSSH there is measured at build).
decisions: Unix sockets stay the transport inside a Linux box; TCP is added only where Unix cannot go (Windows, box to box).
The wire format (one JSON request, one JSON reply) does not change; callers do not change.
remote.py picks AF_UNIX when socket has it and the bus is on this box, else TCP.
Box to box rides an ssh tunnel with the host key checked; no bus listens on the LAN; on Windows the bus listens on 127.0.0.1 only (open-4d72b5d4dbe0, Akien 2026-11-04).
remote.py spawns the bus on Windows with DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW, as launchers/superclaude _sc_spawn_detached does.
A proof tooth forces the TCP path on Linux (AF_UNIX hidden) so the Windows path is provable on this box.
Bus-to-bus routing by name is out of scope: a follow-on ticket.
